industry: B2B SaaS (Knowledge Management / Customer Support AI)
next_step: Share a daily usage export sample (UTC) including billed_tokens + cache_hit attribution by model/region; confirm overage behavior for proposed mid-market package; schedule technical sign-off on dashboard + reconciliation flow.
blockers: Wants usage exports to match invoice line items; currently sees small deltas vs in-app usage dashboard due to late-arriving events + cache-hit attribution gaps.
Needs clear customer-facing definition of billed tokens vs raw tokens (esp. retries/fallback + streaming).
Finance team requesting timezone alignment (UTC) and stable schema for ingestion into their warehouse.
activity_timeline: 2026-01-23 — Company created in HubSpot after inbound signup + credits request; noted interest in predictable spend + strong usage reporting.
2026-02-04 — POC kickoff (30m). Northwind asked for: per-model cost breakdown, cache-hit visibility, and daily export they can reconcile to invoice.
2026-02-14 — POC check-in (Fireflies). Reviewed Redwood Console usage tiles; customer flagged mismatch between dashboard totals and their internal token counter (streaming + retries).
2026-02-19 — Follow-up email: asked whether cached responses are billed; requested a field that distinguishes billed vs raw tokens and cache-hit attribution in export.
2026-02-25 — Commercial check-in: discussed moving from credits to a package with included tokens and overage; asked for guardrails (hard cap vs soft overage) + alerting when nearing limits.
requirements_summary: Workload: RAG-based support agent + doc search (embeddings) + summarization jobs. Latency target: p95 < 800ms for chat (short prompts), embeddings can be batch/async. Throughput: bursts during business hours; wants guidance on caching/batching to manage cost. Model needs: prefers a stable default model with fallback option (customer said: "we can accept a slightly smaller fallback model if it keeps us online"). Metering/reporting: strong emphasis on finance-grade telemetry—daily usage export in UTC, by model + region, with separate prompt/completion/billed token fields; wants cache-hit attribution shown and ideally excluded from billed usage if policy is to not charge cached tokens (they will accept either policy but want it explicit). Retries/streaming semantics: needs clarity on whether partial streams count, and how server-side retries/fallback affect billed tokens (concern about double-charging). Security: SOC 2 is table stakes; wants audit logging and a clear retention policy for usage/billing logs to satisfy their own internal controls.
packaging_preferences: Preference for a mid-market "included usage + overage" package vs pure pay-as-you-go. They want: (1) included monthly token bundle sized to current POC plus 30–50% headroom, (2) predictable overage rate, (3) alerts at 50/80/95% of included usage, and (4) a hard cap option for safety during early rollout. Asked specifically whether embeddings are metered per input item when batching (they batch many short strings) and want the invoice/export to reflect that cleanly.
metering_dashboard_feedback:
Console feedback: usage dashboard is helpful but they want drilldowns by (model, region, endpoint) and a single "billed usage" number that matches invoicing. Current pain points reported during POC: 
- "Billed vs raw tokens" confusion (their internal counter differs, esp. for streaming).
- Cache attribution not visible end-to-end; they want a cache_hit flag + cached_tokens/raw_tokens/billed_tokens in exports.
- Retries/fallback: asked for an explicit statement that tokens are not double-counted on server retry; they referenced seeing spikes on days with higher error rates.
- Export format: wants a stable schema suitable for ingestion into their warehouse; daily partitions; UTC boundaries; include request_id/idempotency_key where possible for reconciliation.
- Timezone: their finance reporting is standardized on UTC; they had a prior vendor where local-time exports caused day-over-day spikes and disputes.
internal_notes:
POC is progressing; risk is largely around billing trust + reporting. Northwind’s PM/finance stakeholder is highly sensitive to discrepancies and will slow/stop rollout if exports don’t reconcile to invoice. Nadia (Telemetry) to ensure we can provide: billed_tokens fields + cache_hit attribution + clear definition of streaming token accounting. Recommend we treat them as an early design partner for the Usage API fields (they’re willing to test new export schema in parallel). 

Notable quote from 2/14 call: "If our usage export doesn't match the invoice, we get dragged into finance meetings. I need one number that is the number." 

Ask from Jordan (owner): propose package options with explicit overage behavior and a short FAQ snippet explaining billed vs raw tokens + caching + retries in plain English for their internal rollout doc.
data_exports_requested: Daily usage export (UTC) with: account_id, day, endpoint (chat/embeddings), model, region, requests, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, raw_total_tokens, billed_tokens, cache_hit (boolean), cached_tokens (if available), retry_count (server/client if distinguishable), and a stable unique request identifier for dedupe/reconciliation. They also asked whether a Snowflake-native share is possible long-term; short term OK with CSV/Parquet in object storage as long as schema is stable and documented.
